target.title: fix(shared): nested gitignore patterns over-anchored and escaped ! corrupted
target.body:
Fixes #106249

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`, which rewrites nested ignore-file patterns incorrectly:

1. Slash-free patterns in nested `.gitignore`/`.ignore`/`.fdignore` files were over-anchored, so files deeper in the subdirectory were not ignored even though git would ignore them.
2. Escaped `!` (`\!`) patterns were stripped to bare `!`, which the `ignore` library treats as negation instead of a literal filename at the root level.

This affects skill/file discovery paths that rely on these matchers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gitignore semantics say a pattern without a slash matches at any depth below the directory containing the ignore file. A pattern with a slash (beginning or middle) is anchored to that directory. `addIgnoreRules` was prefixing all patterns directly (`sub/*.log`), which the `ignore` library treats as anchored. It was also stripping the `\!` escape, causing the `ignore` library to read it as negation.

The fix:

- Adds `**/` before slash-free patterns when a nested prefix exists (`sub/**/*.log`).
- Keeps escaped `\!` intact so the `ignore` library treats it as a literal filename.
- Still anchors patterns that contain a beginning or middle slash.

## User Impact

Skills, prompts, themes, and extension trees that contain nested `.gitignore` files with unanchored patterns now correctly exclude ignored files from deeper subdirectory levels. Escaped `!` filenames are no longer silently re-included.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Before the fix, `addIgnoreRules` on a nested `.gitignore` containing `*.log`:

```text
sub/y.log     -> true
sub/deep/x.log -> false   # should be true
```

After the fix:

```text
sub/y.log     -> true
sub/deep/x.log -> true
```

Verified against real `git check-ignore` in a temp repo:

```text
$ git check-ignore sub/y.log sub/deep/x.log
sub/y.log
sub/deep/x.log
```

For the `\!` escape, the old code stripped the backslash and turned `\!keep.txt` into a negation, which un-ignored `keep.txt`. The new code preserves `\!keep.txt` so the `ignore` library matches a literal `!keep.txt` file.

### Automated tests

Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` covering:

- nested slash-free patterns at any depth
- anchored middle-slash patterns
- leading-slash anchored patterns
- trailing-slash directory patterns
- escaped `!` at the root
- escaped `!` in nested directories

### Validation run

- `pnpm test src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run` → 6/6 passed
- `pnpm test src/shared --run` → 47 files, 468 tests passed
- `pnpm format:check src/shared/ignore-rules.ts src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` → clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.ts src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` → 0 warnings, 0 errors
